stories.title: Dextrose prolotherapy plus steroid eases tennis elbow pain early
stories.summary: A retrospective study found that combining corticosteroid injections with hypertonic dextrose prolotherapy provided better short-term pain relief and reduced tendon thickness compared to prolotherapy alone. The advantage faded by the 12 and 24 week marks. The elbow eventually decides how it feels regardless of the initial strategy.

stories.title: Engineered protein targets Alzheimer's-linked brain deposits
stories.summary: A KAIST-led research team identified a protein capable of suppressing the harmful aggregation of amyloid-beta, a peptide associated with Alzheimer's disease. The approach also reduced the toxicity of existing protein aggregates. The research suggests a potential therapeutic avenue for clearing the brain of these specific deposits.

stories.title: Personalized vaccine targets melanoma recurrence
stories.summary: Sutter Health investigators are participating in a study of a personalized cancer vaccine designed to prevent melanoma from returning after surgery. The trial aims to determine if the treatment can effectively reduce recurrence rates. The full details of the study are available to subscribers.

stories.title: 'Gatekeeper' cells can restrict the immune response to cancer
stories.summary: A King's College London study found that chemotherapy helps attract stem-like T cells toward tumors. However, macrophages surrounding tumor blood vessels can act as a barrier, limiting the ability of these T cells to reach the cancer. The immune system is being asked to fight behind a wall.

stories.title: 'Mini lens' grown in lab could help tackle cataracts
stories.summary: Scientists from Anglia Ruskin University and colleagues in Japan have grown a realistic human lens in a laboratory setting. This development offers a potential new path for treating cataracts, one of the leading causes of blindness worldwide. The eye has been successfully replicated in miniature.

stories.title: Slug-inspired gel seals digestive tract fistulas in animal tests
stories.summary: Gastrointestinal fistulas, which are abnormal passages between the digestive tract and other organs, can be life-threatening complications of surgery or trauma. Researchers are testing a slug-inspired gel designed to seal these passages. The full report on these animal tests is available to subscribers.

stories.title: Stronger cholesterol treatment shrinks more plaque in heart arteries
stories.summary: A new clinical trial has found that more intensive cholesterol treatment leads to a greater reduction of plaque in heart arteries. The study provides additional data on the relationship between cholesterol management and arterial health. The full findings are available to subscribers.

stories.title: Early IgG drops may predict treatment response in generalized MG
stories.summary: An analysis suggests that early drops in immunoglobulin G levels may predict short-term improvement in patients with generalized myasthenia gravis treated with batoclimab. Researchers note that while these drops may serve as a useful indicator, more research is required to confirm their predictive value.

stories.title: Perioperative ivonescimab shows promising responses in lung cancer
stories.summary: A phase II study published in Nature Medicine reports that neoadjuvant ivonescimab combined with chemotherapy achieved a 70.1 percent major pathological response rate in resectable lung cancer. The treatment demonstrated a manageable safety profile. The cancer is being asked to respond to a dual-targeting antibody.

stories.title: Triplet therapy shows promise in early bladder cancer study
stories.summary: A three-drug combination of sacituzumab govitecan, enfortumab vedotin and zimberelimab showed manageable toxicity and antitumor activity in patients with previously untreated metastatic urothelial cancer. The results were presented at the 2026 ESMO Congress. The drugs were described as manageable by the study authors.

stories.title: Targeted scan detects hidden multiple myeloma
stories.summary: A phase 2 clinical trial found that a targeted immunoPET scan detected active multiple myeloma that standard PET/CT scans and blood tests missed. The findings could help doctors map disease and confirm if cancer remains after therapy. Multiple myeloma is a disease that can remain hidden in plain sight.

stories.title: Treatment satisfaction higher for patients choosing their own care
stories.summary: A study indicates that patients with rheumatoid arthritis report higher treatment satisfaction when they are involved in choosing their own therapy. The research highlights the role of patient preference in clinical outcomes. The full details of the study are available to subscribers.

stories.title: Air pollution linked to over 2 million deaths in India in 2023
stories.summary: A report by FICCI and EY attributes more than two million deaths in India to air pollution in 2023. Exposure to fine particulate matter is linked to respiratory illnesses, heart disease and cognitive impairment. The report warns of significant impacts on healthcare expenditure and economic productivity.

stories.title: Air pollution costs India up to 9.5 percent of GDP
stories.summary: A new report links air pollution to two million deaths in India and estimates the economic cost at up to 9.5 percent of the country's GDP. The study calls for health-led action to address the crisis. The full details are available to subscribers.

stories.title: Health ministry proposes Schedule M amendments
stories.summary: The health ministry has proposed amendments to Schedule M, which outlines good manufacturing practices for pharmaceutical products. The proposal aims to update standards for the industry. The full text of the proposed changes is available to subscribers.

stories.title: Ministry proposes suspension for substandard drug manufacturers
stories.summary: The Union Health Ministry has proposed the immediate suspension of manufacturing licenses for drugs found to be of substandard quality on specified critical parameters. The move is intended to address quality concerns within the pharmaceutical sector. The full details are available to subscribers.

stories.title: FICCI-EY paper urges India to embed PM2.5 targets in policy
stories.summary: A paper from FICCI and EY recommends that India integrate specific PM2.5 targets into its national clean air policy. The authors argue that such measures are necessary to address the health consequences of fine particulate matter. The full paper is available to subscribers.

stories.title: Climate change driving early deliveries in India
stories.summary: An exceptionally hot April in 2024 was associated with 10,050 additional preterm births in India. Analysis by Zero Carbon Analytics suggests that by mid-century, climate change could drive over 15,300 excess preterm births during an ordinary April. The weather is becoming a public health challenge.

stories.title: ICMR seeks dust control for combine harvester operators
stories.summary: The Indian Council of Medical Research has called for research into measures to reduce dust exposure for combine harvester workers. Operators frequently inhale crop and soil particles, which can lead to respiratory damage. The council is now seeking practical solutions to protect those working in the fields.

stories.title: Health Ministry proposes immediate licence suspension for substandard drugs
stories.summary: The Union Health Ministry has proposed amendments to the Drugs Rules, 1945, to allow for the immediate suspension of manufacturing licences for drugs deemed not of standard quality. The move aims to enable prompt regulatory intervention, replacing current procedures that often involve lengthy delays before taking action.

stories.title: Health Ministry moves to bypass delays for drug quality failures
stories.summary: The Union Ministry of Health and Family Welfare has proposed amendments to the Drugs Rules, 1945, to immediately suspend manufacturing licences for drugs failing critical quality tests. The change removes the requirement for lengthy show-cause procedures, allowing for faster regulatory intervention when substandard medicines are detected.

stories.title: Health Ministry aligns microbial monitoring with WHO standards
stories.summary: The Health Ministry has proposed amendments to the Drugs Rules, 1945, to align microbial monitoring in sterile manufacturing areas with World Health Organization guidelines. Any microbial growth detected in critical Grade A zones will now trigger a formal investigation to ensure compliance with international good manufacturing practices.

stories.title: Experts challenge double-fortified salt plan for anaemia
stories.summary: Public health experts have criticised a proposal to expand the use of double-fortified salt to combat anaemia. In an open letter, they warned that adding iron to iodised salt ignores multiple underlying causes of the condition. India continues to struggle with anaemia despite years of various fortification efforts.

stories.title: Wisconsin reports first measles death in 36 years
stories.summary: Wisconsin health officials have confirmed the death of an infant from measles, the state's first such fatality since 1990. The Department of Health Services provided no further details to protect the family's privacy. Measles is a vaccine-preventable disease that was declared eliminated in the United States in 2000.

stories.title: Infant's death linked to measles outbreak in southwest Wisconsin
stories.summary: Wisconsin health officials reported the death of an infant related to the ongoing measles outbreak in southwestern Wisconsin. stories.title: WHO recommends new Ebola vaccine candidates for DRC trial
stories.summary: World Health Organization advisers have recommended two experimental vaccines for testing against the Bundibugyo virus in the Democratic Republic of the Congo. The candidates, developed by Oxford and Moderna, will be included in the ongoing Tumaini clinical trial to address a virus that current vaccines do not cover.

stories.title: Review finds digital health effective but not superior to standard care
stories.summary: An umbrella review of 232 publications found that digital health interventions are effective when compared to doing nothing. However, the study of over 550,000 participants showed that digital tools generally match, rather than exceed, the benefits of standard clinical therapies across a wide range of medical conditions.

stories.title: Avanlee Care raises $3.5 million for caregiver platform
stories.summary: Avanlee Care has raised $3.5 million in seed funding to expand its platform for family caregivers into the Medicare Advantage market. The company helps health plans engage caregivers to manage medications and appointments. This latest round brings the startup's total funding to $6 million.

stories.title: MindInventory expands its healthcare software services
stories.summary: MindInventory has extended its healthcare IT offerings to include end-to-end, AI-driven digital health solutions for hospitals and clinics. The company provides services for telehealth, EHR integration, and revenue cycle management. The firm says its new suite is designed to meet HIPAA requirements while supporting digital health companies.

stories.title: Rivia launches AI module for clinical trial data
stories.summary: Rivia has released Data Findings, an AI-powered module designed to automate clinical trial data reviews and reduce development delays. The tool integrates with the company's existing platform to identify and track data issues. Rivia raised $15 million in Series A funding earlier this year.

stories.title: New York digital health funding rises 36 percent
stories.summary: New York City digital health startups raised $1.9 billion in the third quarter of 2026, a 36 percent increase year over year. Nationally, U.S. startups raised $3.7 billion across 114 deals during the same period. Buyers are now assessing which vendors are pulling ahead in the market.

stories.title: Clinics On Cloud raises funding after eight years
stories.summary: Pune-based Clinics On Cloud has secured its first outside investment, raising 120 crore rupees at a 600 crore rupee valuation. The Series A round was backed by Dubai-based Model42. The startup, founded in 2018, plans to use the capital to build a worldwide network of microclinics.

stories.title: Clinics On Cloud raises USD 12.5M in Series A round
stories.summary: Company News Clinics On Cloud raises USD 12.5M in Series A round Indian healthtech startup Clinics On Cloud has raised $12.5 million in a Series A funding round from investors in Dubai. The company plans to use the funds to expand its healthcare technology business

stories.title: Ayushman Bharat records 11.69 crore hospital admissions
stories.summary: The Ayushman Bharat scheme has authorised 11.69 crore hospital admissions as of February 2026, with 6.74 crore occurring in private facilities. The government maintains a centralised grievance system for patients to report treatment denials. Strict guidelines are in place to ensure hospitals provide care to all beneficiaries.

stories.title: Trust, relationships and funding gaps shape mental health implementation
stories.summary: Researchers have examined how a national network set up to bridge the gap between mental health research and practice supported the adoption and evaluation of evidence-based interventions across England, and their analysis points to relationships, communication and time as the factors that mattered most. stories.title: Study finds childhood obesity risk may be reversible
stories.summary: A study of 368,756 adults published in the Journal of Affective Disorders suggests that risks of depression and anxiety linked to childhood obesity may reset to normal levels if a healthy adult weight is achieved. The findings offer a qualified message of hope for parents of struggling children.

stories.title: Wearable monitoring in mental health care: scoping review finds limited
stories.summary: Wearable technologies designed to monitor people receiving mental health care are advancing rapidly and attracting significant international investment, yet the evidence supporting their use remains limited and the ethical, legal and policy questions surrounding them remain largely unresolved. That is the central conclusion of a

stories.title: Chilean school communities see teen mental health as widespread but respond
stories.summary: Chilean secondary school communities describe adolescent mental health in two very different registers at once: as emotional well-being to be nurtured, and as a landscape of problems, diagnoses, treatments and specialized care. That dual picture comes from an interpretive qualitative study that analyzed social representations

stories.title: COVID-19-related stress linked to faster epigenetic aging in adolescents
stories.summary: 🛡️ Just a quick check We’re checking your connection to prevent automated abuse The COVID-19 pandemic and its associated measures caused significant stress across all levels of society, negatively impacting physical and mental health. The biological consequences of this stress have not yet been explored.

stories.title: Meditation study shows no advantage over relaxation
stories.summary: A four-week trial found that loving-kindness meditation did not outperform progressive muscle relaxation in reducing pain or improving social well-being. Participants practicing muscle relaxation reported higher perceived social support. Neither practice proved superior for pain management, though increased social support was linked to higher pain endurance at follow-up.

stories.title: Lancet Study: 1 In 4 Adolescents Worldwide Report No Active Days Every Week: What Are The Health Risks?
stories.summary: SummaryThe Lancet study finds that 240 million young people worldwide report no active days every week, with girls less active than boys. Researchers highlight persistent gender gaps, safety concerns and barriers to physical activity, calling for policies that encourage healthier, more active lifestyles.

stories.title: Online sports betting linked to increased mental health service use
stories.summary: A study in JAMA Psychiatry analyzed 62 million insurance enrollee-years and found that states legalizing online sports betting saw increases in mental health medication use and outpatient care. The researchers suggest that expanding betting access may create additional demand for services. The house always wins, eventually.

research.title: Goodbye, cavities? Scientists create gel that could regrow tooth enamel
research.summary: Scientists have developed a revolutionary gel that could regrow lost tooth enamel by harnessing minerals naturally found in saliva, potentially overcoming one of dentistry’s biggest limitations. The regenerated enamel behaves much like healthy enamel, raising hopes for a simple treatment that could repair damaged teeth, prevent decay, and.

research.title: Scientists solve 30-year-old mystery and discover a hidden defense against inflammation
research.summary: Scientists have solved a decades-old mystery and uncovered a hidden immune system defense that protects healthy cells from the very inflammation meant to fight infections. The surprising discovery could lead to new approaches for treating cancer, inflammatory bowel disease, and other conditions involving excessive inflammation.

research.title: Scientists turn viruses into weapons against deadly superbugs
research.summary: Scientists are advancing a promising new way to fight antibiotic-resistant infections by using viruses that specifically target and kill harmful bacteria. An international team has released the first coordinated guidelines for personalized phage therapy, offering a roadmap for safely bringing this experimental treatment into clinical practice. Early findings.

research.title: The cow, the flea and the genome: One Health and the statecraft of prevention
research.summary: A cattle virus at home and a plague scare abroad make the same argument this World One Health Day: life is epidemiologically indivisible, and the institutions that govern and study it must learn to be so too

research.title: Even moderate drinking linked to cancer and early death, major study finds
research.summary: A major new study challenges the idea that moderate drinking is safe, finding that even relatively small amounts of alcohol increase the risk of cancer, heart disease, and premature death. Researchers found no overall health benefits from drinking and warn that consuming more than one alcoholic beverage per.

research.title: New diabetes implant uses electricity to lower blood sugar and promote weight loss
research.summary: Researchers have developed a remarkable new electronic implant that could transform type 2 diabetes treatment by lowering blood sugar without insulin or traditional drugs. The device uses a special electrically powered catalyst to convert excess glucose into a substance that the body eliminates through urine, potentially preventing unwanted.

research.title: Common pesticide linked to 2.5 times the risk of Parkinson’s disease
research.summary: A UCLA study found that long-term exposure to a common pesticide was linked to more than 2.5 times the risk of Parkinson's disease. Scientists also uncovered how the chemical damages brain cells and identified a promising way to protect them.

research.title: Drinking tea may help protect your heart, but there’s a surprising catch
research.summary: A massive study of nearly 486,000 adults found that regularly drinking tea was associated with an 11% lower risk of heart and blood vessel diseases. The lowest risk was linked to drinking roughly six to eight cups per day, with black tea showing more consistent benefits than green.
